summary: Iteration 17 — P0 per-ride authorization: 19/19 backend tests passed. Verified ensure_ride_participant, ensure_ride_customer, ensure_thread_access + driver-status ownership for all listed endpoints, plus regression happy-path for owner (create→offers→select→track→cancel) and driver (online→bid→active→driver-status). Registered a fresh attacker customer and confirmed 403 responses for every cross-user access attempt while owners/admins/assigned drivers get 200.
critical_code_review_comments: ensure_ride_participant, ensure_ride_customer, ensure_thread_access are clean, small, and consistently used at the top of every affected route in server.py (~L363-388).
is_ride_driver correctly matches both assigned_driver.id and driver_bid.driver_id so an assigned/bidding driver keeps access after selection.
Support thread rule (`support-<userId>`) enforced by string prefix + exact-id match — attacker cannot read/post to another user's support-<id> and admin bypass works.
seed_data_creation: One-off attacker customer registered per test session: TEST_attacker_<uuid>@getaride.com / Attack1234 (via /api/auth/register). No production data mutated.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter17 added authorization helpers (ensure_ride_participant / ensure_ride_customer / ensure_thread_access) and they all pass. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_iter17_ride_authorization.py can be reused as a regression suite for any future ride/chat endpoint changes.
